title: Hollow and Oath
premise: In the valley of Hollowmere, where magic cannot cross the boundary stones, Cyrus Iversen has lived his whole life believing he was ordinary—the last apprentice of a guild that once guarded kings. When crown hunters arrive seeking anyone with 'the gift,' Cyrus learns his guild's dying magic lives dormant in him, and that the king himself is bound to a memory-eating entity wearing his crown. Fleeing with two fellow apprentices who become the family he never had, Cyrus must reach the capital and unbind the king before the entity consumes every memory of magic from the world—including his own. In the end, Cyrus defeats the entity not by destroying it but by giving it his most painful memory, freeing the king at the cost of forgetting his dead mother's face, and returns to Hollowmere with a found family and a guild reborn.
about_author: Freya Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval guild records before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about institutions, inheritance, and the people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Crown hunters arrive in Hollowmere asking questions about the old Guild of the Bound Oath, and Cyrus discovers the guild sigil burned into his palm glows when they pass—proof he carries the gift he never knew he had. His master, dying, reveals the guild's true purpose: binding things that eat memories. The emotional beat is the shattering of a safe, small life.

chapters.title: Three Names on an Oath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Cyrus and Wren, a sharp-tongued fellow apprentice. The three surviving apprentices flee over the boundary stones, where magic floods into Cyrus painfully for the first time. Hunted through the lowlands, they forge bonds of trust through shared danger, and Wren teaches Cyrus to shape his gift. The emotional beat is found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV during the infiltration of the capital. They witness the king—hollow-eyed, repeating the same day of memories—and meet the entity, called the Tithe, which offers Cyrus power in exchange for abandoning his companions. When their plan collapses and one companion is captured, Cyrus must choose: flee or bargain. The emotional beat is temptation and sacrifice at the climax's edge.

chapters.title: What Memory Owes
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the throne room, Cyrus performs the unbinding rite, but the Tithe demands a memory of equal weight to release the king. Cyrus surrenders his memory of his mother's face, breaking the entity's hold and freeing both king and kingdom. He wakes in Hollowmere, unable to recall her smile but surrounded by his chosen family as the guild lights its first new fire. The emotional beat is grief transmuted into belonging.
